# Ellen West

[Episcopalians](../codex/factions.md#episcopalians)

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P29](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0029), [v5 CHAPTER XXII. ST. GEORGE KNOWS ALL ABOUT IT P8](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0008), [v5 CHAPTER XXII. ST. GEORGE KNOWS ALL ABOUT IT P40](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0040)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_
- **Family:** [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) (relative), [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) (spouse), [Rosemary West](../character/rosemary-west.md) (sibling)

## Appearance

Ellen West is a dark and massive woman with black hair, thick black eyebrows, and clear, slaty blue eyes. Although she possesses a stern and forbidding look along with a deep voice, she is actually very jolly.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P54](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0054), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025)_

## Personality

Ellen is noted for being a loyal and dependable person who can also behave tyrannically toward others while indulging them. Beneath this demeanor, she is naturally very jolly, possessing a hearty, gurgling laugh and a deep, pleasant voice.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 CHAPTER XXXIV. UNA VISITS THE HILL P6](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0006)_

## History

Ellen West discussed European politics with [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) when he visited her home. When she suspected he was interested in courting her sister [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md), she reminded [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) of a solemn pact they had made ten years earlier never to marry. When [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) later asked to be released from this vow following John's marriage proposal, Ellen fiercely refused, forcing [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) to reject him. Later, after [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) asked to marry Ellen, [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) agreed to release her from her promise, but Ellen ultimately refused to marry Norman after realizing it would leave [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) living alone.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P5](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0005), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P12](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0012), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P19](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0019), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P31](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0031), [v5 CHAPTER XXII. ST. GEORGE KNOWS ALL ABOUT IT P1](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0001), [v5 CHAPTER XXII. ST. GEORGE KNOWS ALL ABOUT IT P21](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0021), +6 more_

**Volume 5**

## Quotes

> "I will not do it. A promise is a promise in my eyes. I will not do it. Break your promise—be forsworn if you will—but it shall not be with any assent of mine."
>
> — Ellen West — [v5 CHAPTER XXII. ST. GEORGE KNOWS ALL ABOUT IT P28](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0028)

> "Mark my words, Mr. Meredith, that man is going to fight somebody yet. He’s aching to. He is going to set the world on fire."
>
> — Ellen West — [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P27](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0027)

> “Then,” said Ellen coldly, and determinedly, “I shall not marry him. I shall not leave you here alone. That is all there is to be said about it.”
>
> — Ellen West — [v5 CHAPTER XXXII. TWO STUBBORN PEOPLE P41](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0041)

> "It is not nonsense. It is my firm decision. It would be absurd for you to think of living here by yourself—a mile from any other house. If you won’t come with me I’ll stay with you. Now, we won’t argue the matter, so don’t try."
>
> — Ellen West — [v5 CHAPTER XXXII. TWO STUBBORN PEOPLE P43](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0043)

> "When you howl you’re hit, I’ve always heard, George. But she promised, Saint—she promised, and we Wests always keep our word. So it won’t matter if he does want to philander, George. She promised. I won’t worry."
>
> — Ellen West — [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P40](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0040)

## Relationships

### [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/ellen-west--john-meredith.md)

Ellen and [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) are good friends who enjoy easy conversations and humor together, such as discussing European politics and [German](../codex/factions.md#german) militarism in her home. However, tension exists because Ellen suspects John of courting her sister [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) and firmly reminds [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) of a past vow that threatens to block any potential marriage between John and [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md).

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P5](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0005), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P12](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0012), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P19](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0019), +5 more_

- Friend of — good friends who share conversations and humor  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XXI. THE IMPOSSIBLE WORD P8](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0008)</sub>

### [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/ellen-west--norman-douglas.md)

Ellen and [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) share a romantic relationship and intend to marry, having resumed their courtship after years apart and enjoying lively arguments with one another. However, their future together hits a snag when Norman tries to resolve the sisters' past promises so he and Ellen can wed. Although [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) agrees to release Ellen, Ellen ultimately refuses to marry Norman because she refuses to leave her sister living alone.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XV. MORE GOSSIP P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 CHAPTER XXII. ST. GEORGE KNOWS ALL ABOUT IT P1](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0001), [v5 CHAPTER XXII. ST. GEORGE KNOWS ALL ABOUT IT P21](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0021), +12 more_

- Romantically involved with — courting again after years apart  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XV. MORE GOSSIP P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 CHAPTER XXII. ST. ### [Rosemary West](../character/rosemary-west.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/ellen-west--rosemary-west.md)

Ellen and [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) are sisters bound by a solemn vow made ten years prior never to marry so they could live together. When [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) proposes to [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md), Ellen fiercely refuses to release her sister from this promise, forcing [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) to send him a heartbreak-inducing rejection. Though Ellen later experiences remorse and even offers to stay unmarried herself so [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) won't be left alone, their mutual pact creates significant friction around both of their marital prospects.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P50](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0050), [v5 CHAPTER XII. AN EXPLANATION AND A DARE P5](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0005), +22 more_

- Sibling of — sisters who vowed to live together  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P50](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0050), [v5 CHAPTER XII. AN EXPLANATION AND A DARE P5](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0005), +8 more</sub>
